text:
Maya: Hey — hitting a weird TS typing divergence between ESM and CJS builds for the JS SDK when targeting the edge runtime. ESM bundle typechecks fine, CJS build complains about overload resolution.

Liam: ugh. do you have a minimal repro? module/tsconfig differences maybe?

Maya: Pasted simplified signatures here — the SDK exposes two overloads for `createClient`:
```ts
function createClient<T extends object>(opts: { auth: T, retry?: number }): ClientWithAuth<T>
function createClient(opts: { auth: string, retry?: number }): ClientWithAuth<{ token: string }>
```
When I call `createClient({ auth: process.env.AUTH })` in an ESM + tsconfig moduleResolution: "nodeNext" build, inference picks the string overload (fine). In a CJS-targeted build (tsc -> CommonJS) it tries to pick the generic overload and `T` becomes `any` which then leaks and later errors out in the edge runtime.

Sasha: Are you bundling? esbuild/rollup can change how `typeof process` is emitted which drives TS inference sometimes. Also `skipLibCheck`/`strict` flags matter.

Maya: I'm not bundling for the repro (just tsc + node loader). The repo tsconfig is near-default: `target: ES2020, module: CommonJS` for the CJS path and `module: ESNext` for ESM. I noticed `moduleResolution: node` vs `nodeNext` changes how conditional types resolve — might be related.

Liam: any chance the SDK's index.d.ts has `export =` vs `export default` differences between builds? That can alter how overloads merge.

Maya: Good call. Our build pipeline emits `.cjs` shim that uses `module.exports =` and we also ship an ESM `export default`. TS consumers using `esModuleInterop` end up with different inference.

Sasha: Quick checklist: (1) try `moduleResolution: nodeNext` for CJS build too; (2) enable `preserveValueImports`? (3) make overloads less ambiguous with a discriminant like `authType: 'token' | 'credentials'` so inference doesn't guess.

Maya: Tried option 1 — switching CJS build to `nodeNext` made the CJS compiler pick the string overload like ESM. Bad side: downstream customers on older bundlers hit runtime interop issues.

Liam: Maybe adjust the SDK typings so the ambiguous case is resolved at compile time: e.g., add a narrow second overload that accepts `auth: string | number` then a generic fallback that requires an explicit type param. That preserves ergonomics for most users but avoids accidental `any` inference.

Maya: Thinking to land a change: make the generic overload require `createClient<T>(opts: ClientOptionsWithAuth<T>)` only when `auth` is an object literal or `as const` — otherwise prefer primitive overload. But not sure how to encode that in TS cleanly.

Sasha: You can use conditional overload ordering: put the primitive/string overload above the generic one so TS prefers it when it matches. Also include a comment in CHANGELOG about tsconfig interplay.

Maya: Will draft a small PR with reordered overloads + an example in docs showing `tsconfig` recommendations for edge consumers (nodeNext / module: ESNext) and a note for CJS packagers.

devx-bot: New PR draft created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412 — includes overload reorder + tsconfig note. CI: run-infra/unit-types: pending. :eyes:

Liam: Awesome. Once CI is green can we add a small sample in `examples/edge-hello` showing recommended tsconfig for edge SDK usage? That will help support tickets.

Maya: Yep — will add sample and a snippet to the onboarding guide about `unknown` vs `any` pitfalls (callsites that rely on `any` will break in strict mode at the edge).

Sasha: If support tickets keep coming, we can add a runtime parity check in the Console that warns when a consumer bundle uses the CJS interop pattern. Low friction.

Maya: Thanks y'all. PR link above, I'll shepherd through fixes and add the example.

Liam: Thx — very devx-friendly. Keep us posted. :thumbsup:
